clue.text: One and only trendy Di taking exercise initially — needs a cure for poor circulation?

definitions.text: needs a cure for poor circulation

parts.note: the, stressed, means the unique or pre-eminent one
in means fashionable
taken as written

indicators.note: says to take just the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the word whose opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Princess Diana, unique and fashionable, takes up exercise and is advised to improve her blood flow.
explanation.walkthrough: The Indie is a nickname for The Independent, a British daily paper that was struggling with low sales in the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: The Independent newspaper sold relatively few copies, so it needed remedies for its weak readership.

clue.text: One politician embracing girl gets erection, the bloody sap

indicators.note: in a down answer, putting it upright means reading it from bottom to top

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: the politician's letters hold the girl's name between them

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A politician clinches a girl and is aroused, the bloody fool.
explanation.walkthrough: The bloody sap looks like an insult; it means the fluid part of blood, the body's sap.
explanation.definitionFit: Plasma is the liquid component of blood, likened to the sap that flows through a plant.

clue.text: Work situation required for the Tories now!

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a position is a situation or job

explanation.surface: A job vacancy for the Conservatives, needed urgently.
explanation.walkthrough: After losing the 1997 general election, the Conservatives became the main party not in government.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest party not in government in Parliament, which the Conservatives became after losing power in 1997.

clue.text: Apercentage of Brenda's sort of people

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fee paid to an author or patent holder as a share of sales
second meaning: Private Eye's Brenda is the Queen, so her kind are royal persons

explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye calls the Queen Brenda.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a share of sales paid to a writer and royal persons collectively.

clue.text: Royal makes date whatever's around

indicators.note: the word for whatever goes round the date letter

parts.note: any means whatever, as in any one; the 's is short for is

explanation.surface: A prince fixes up a date with whoever is available.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Andrew was widely known as Andy.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Andrew, the Queen's second son, is a member of the royal family.

clue.text: Our regular look at erections, endless sex on beach (tricky positions)

definitions.note: phrased as a plural column, so the answer is a column title, not a plural noun

indicators.note: the slang word loses its final letter

parts.note: nooky is slang for sex
sand is what a beach is made of
corners are awkward spots, as in being in a tight corner

explanation.surface: Private Eye promotes its smutty survey of sex on the beach in awkward poses.
explanation.walkthrough: Nooks and Corners is Private Eye's long-running architecture column; erections are buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: Nooks and Corners is Private Eye's regular column criticising new building work.

clue.text: Superannuated, clapped out bowler?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: outdated, behind the times
second meaning, literally: a worn-out bowler hat

explanation.walkthrough: Bowler suggests cricket; it is the round felt hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means outdated or stale, and literally describes a worn, aged hat.

clue.text: The other half of Brenda's tonic, it's said

indicators.note: tells us the word for a tonic is only to be heard, and the answer is a different word that sounds the same

parts.note: a fillip is a boost or stimulus, something that acts as a tonic

explanation.surface: Private Eye jokes about the Queen's husband as the gin to go with her tonic.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye calls the Queen Brenda, so her other half is her husband, Prince Philip.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Philip was the husband, or other half, of Queen Elizabeth II, whom Private Eye nicknamed Brenda.

clue.text: Wogan revived with external oxygen line — for which the other side's most grateful!

definitions.text: for which the other side's most grateful

indicators.note: the oxygen and line letters sit on the outside, one at each end of the rearranged name

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol

indicators.note: brought back to life in a new form, so the letters of the name are rearranged

parts.note: Terry Wogan, the broadcaster; his name supplies the letters

explanation.surface: Terry Wogan being revived with an oxygen line, to the relief of someone on the other side.
explanation.walkthrough: In football an own goal is scored by a player into their own net, a gift to the opposing team.
explanation.definitionFit: An own goal counts for the opposing team, so it is a mistake the opponents are especially thankful for.

clue.text: Roger conventionally taking this view that pagan foreigners should be converted?

definitions.meaning: to roger is British slang for having sex, and the conventional way to do it is in this sexual posture

definitions.text: view that pagan foreigners should be converted
definitions.meaning: read literally, the stance held by an evangelist sent abroad to bring heathens to Christianity

explanation.surface: A churchy statement of belief that heathens abroad should be brought to the faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Roger is British slang for having sex; the answer is both the most ordinary sexual posture and, taken literally, a missionary's opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: The missionary position is the conventional face-to-face sexual posture, and punningly the stance taken by evangelists abroad.

clue.text: Punch affiliated to hard left! — premier

parts.note: KO is a knockout, the result of a decisive punch

explanation.surface: A political figure with a punch, signed up to the hard left.
explanation.walkthrough: Helmut Kohl was German Chancellor in 1997, so a head of government; the surface's hard left is a red herring for him, a Christian Democrat.
explanation.definitionFit: Helmut Kohl led Germany as Chancellor, the country's head of government, which is what a premier is.

clue.text: Treated as dirt, without interest, John Major is no longer ours

definitions.text: John Major is no longer ours

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside: the rearranged letters stand around the interest letter
these letters are processed or worked on, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
i is the symbol for an interest rate

explanation.surface: A bitter note that the defeated Prime Minister, scorned and dull, is no longer the nation's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye ran The Secret Diary of John Major, a spoof diary that ended when he lost the 1997 election, so his diarist was no longer theirs.
explanation.definitionFit: Private Eye's spoof diary was written in John Major's voice, so the writer of a diary describes him as the magazine's former columnist.

clue.text: Boxers entertain a number of pansies possibly

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them inside, so the underwear holds the number

parts.note: boxer shorts are a kind of pants, the British word for underpants
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fighters playing host to a group of effeminate men, in the old slur.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain pants are underpants, so boxers are pants. Pansy is an old insult the surface leans on, but a pansy is also a garden flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Pansies are flowering garden species, examples of vegetation in general, signalled by possibly.

clue.text: Di Spencer's wayward youth in Bill's hands once again

indicators.note: unruly and straying, so the letters go astray into a new order

parts.note: Diana Spencer, Princess of Wales; her name supplies the letters
Y is a recognised abbreviation for youth, as in YMCA

explanation.surface: Princess Diana's rebellious young days are being looked after by Bill again.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill is Bill Clinton, re-elected US President in 1996.
explanation.definitionFit: Clinton won a second term in 1996, so the office of US head of state was his again.

clue.text: What Di likes to do: give the castle a seizure!

parts.note: the keep is the strongest central tower of a castle
a fit is a sudden attack or convulsion

explanation.surface: Princess Diana's habits threaten to give a royal castle a convulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: Diana was famously a regular at the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana was well known for her gym routine, and exercising regularly for health is the everyday phrase for that habit.

clue.text: See 10
Brenda's captivated by new heartthrob, a bit like Mr Bean

indicators.note: held captive, so the Queen's letters are trapped inside the other two pieces

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
Brenda is Private Eye's name for the Queen, whose royal cipher is ER; the 's is short for is

explanation.surface: The Queen falls for a new pin-up who turns out to be rather like Rowan Atkinson's bumbling character.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Bean is Rowan Atkinson's gormless, socially awkward TV character.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Bean is clumsy and socially inept, which is what being somewhat geeky or awkward suggests.

clue.text: Roger, plied with drink, makes a complete balls of it

definitions.text: makes a complete balls of it

indicators.note: the sex word is given a drink, which follows it

parts.note: both roger and screw are slang for having sex
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Roger gets drunk and makes a mess of things.
explanation.walkthrough: Roger looks like a man's name; it is slang for having sex.
explanation.definitionFit: To screw up is to botch something badly, which is what making a balls of it means in British slang.

clue.text: See 6
Cooler, on ship these days?

definitions.meaning: in 1997 Britain moored a floating jail, HMP Weare, at Portland to hold inmates

explanation.walkthrough: Cooler sounds like something to keep drinks chilled on a boat; it is slang for a jail, and in 1997 one was literally a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The cooler is slang for a place of confinement for criminals, and HMP Weare was a floating one.

clue.text: Caught one penetrating screwy peer — the makings of a fruit cake?

definitions.text: the makings of a fruit cake

indicators.note: the two letters push into the muddled word
crazy, so the letters of the word are muddled

parts.note: taken as written
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lord who is barking mad, the stuff a nutcase is made of.
explanation.walkthrough: A fruitcake is slang for a crazy person, which the surface uses; here it is a literal cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe lists the ingredients and method for a dish, the makings of a cake.

clue.text: Ex-luvvie shows interest in ring attached to organ

indicators.note: the ring is fixed on to the front of the organ

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: the interest letter goes inside the organ

parts.note: the liver is a body organ
i is the symbol for an interest rate

explanation.surface: A retired actor takes an interest in a ring fixed to some organ.
explanation.walkthrough: A luvvie is British slang for a gushing theatrical type; Laurence Olivier, the great actor, died in 1989.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was the most celebrated British stage actor, now dead, so a former theatrical star.

clue.text: Virgin operation headed by stupid nit!

indicators.note: in this down answer the jumbled word comes on top
a silly arrangement, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
an act is a deed or operation

explanation.surface: A first-time medical procedure led by a foolish idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: Virgin is an adjective here, as in virgin snow.
explanation.definitionFit: Something virgin is untouched and unspoiled, which is to say whole and undamaged.

clue.text: National Conservative piss artist circles

indicators.note: the drunkard goes round the Conservative letter

parts.note: British slang for a drunkard, which a sot is

explanation.surface: A national Tory drunk going round in circles.
explanation.walkthrough: National is a noun here: a citizen of a country, such as Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scot is a person from Scotland, a citizen of that nation.

clue.text: Silent rotten borough, so-called Hollywood

indicators.note: gone bad, so the letters decay into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a borough is a town with its own corporation

explanation.surface: A rotten borough, a seat with almost no voters, that keeps quiet, gets a mocking nickname.
explanation.walkthrough: A rotten borough was a pre-1832 British constituency with almost no voters; silent films hint at Hollywood.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinseltown is the nickname for the American film industry's home, mocking its glitzy surface.

clue.text: Areal drag for hippies?

definitions.meaning: a real drag is hippie slang for a bore, but a drag is also a puff on a cigarette
hippies smoke cannabis, so their kind of puff is on a joint

explanation.walkthrough: The printed run-together Areal is a real; a real drag is a bore, but here drag means a puff.
explanation.definitionFit: A toke is a single puff of a cannabis joint, the kind of drag associated with hippies.

clue.text: One who roughly puts down a tosser

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who plonks things, setting them down heavily
second meaning: British slang for an idiot or fool

explanation.walkthrough: Tosser and plonker are both British insults for a fool; plonk means to set something down clumsily.
explanation.definitionFit: Plonker is mild British slang for a fool, and literally one who plonks, dumping something down heavily.

clue.text: The gaffer can be relied on to make this member in a good mood

definitions.text: The gaffer can be relied on to make this

parts.note: slang for the penis
up means cheerful, as in feeling up

explanation.surface: A boss who is reliably cheerful, or reliably makes a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaffer looks like a boss or foreman; here it is one who makes gaffes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone prone to gaffes always produces a blunder, which is British slang for a botched job.
